title: Ordered Tate right comparisons agree with canonical scalar extension
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes and morphisms are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings and let $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilate both. On small ordinary etale sites use the constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $\mathcal C_{T,R}=D^b_{ctf}(T_{et},R)$ for the full subcategory of complexes with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, meaning that derived tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer]. Put $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$, and $R_T(d)=R_T(1)^{\otimes d}$ for $d\geq0$, with $R_T(0)=R_T$ [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line].
For a base $S$ let $X_0=S$, $X_{r+1}=\mathbf A^1_{X_r}$, $u_r:X_{r+1}\to X_r$, $p_0=1_S$, $p_{r+1}=p_ru_r$ [def-amb-affine-trace-tower]. On each line write $W_{r,R}=j_r^*q_r^*(-)(1)[2]$, for its standard open chart and projective-line projection. Let $h_r:T_{X_{r+1}}j_{r,A}^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{r,B}^*T_{P_r}$ and $a_r:T_{P_r}q_{r,A}^*(-)(1)[2]\xrightarrow{\sim}q_{r,B}^*T_{X_r}(-)(1)[2]$ be the canonical tensor/pullback, Tate and shift comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and put $a^{u_r}=j_{r,B}^*(a_r)\circ h_r(q_{r,A}^*(-)(1)[2])$. Define $\mathcal G_{0,R}=1$, $\mathcal G_{r+1,R}=W_{r,R}\mathcal G_{r,R}$ and comparisons $A_0=1$, $A_{r+1}=W_{r,B}(A_r)\circ a^{u_r}\mathcal G_{r,A}$. Let
$$I_{d,R}:\mathcal G_{d,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{d,R}=p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]$$
be the ordered right normal form of the affine-space adjunction [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], using canonical pullback composition, Tate pullback and tensor reassociation [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Let $a_{d,K}:T_{X_d}G_{d,A}K\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{d,B}T_SK$ be the direct canonical derived tensor/pullback, Tate and shift comparison. For every $d\geq0$ and $K\in\mathcal C_{S,A}$ the specified maps satisfy
$$I_{d,B,T_SK}\circ A_d(K)=a_{d,K}\circ T_{X_d}(I_{d,A,K}).$$
This is equality of the named morphisms in the derived category, including $I_{0,R}=A_0=a_0=1$, and uses the ordered Tate factors and accumulated even shift $[2d]$.

proof.text: Compute all maps on a common flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K$, provided by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Geometric module inverse image and coefficient extension are ringed-topos pullbacks, so [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] applies to both, including the nonflat map $A\to B$. The Tate sheaves are flat by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]; their degree-zero complexes are K-flat directly because their tensor functors are exact. Tensoring these complexes with the pulled-back $P$ stays flat-term K-flat by [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model]. Shifts preserve this property by reindexing the complex and its acyclic test tensors. Thus every successive tensor, scalar extension and pullback in the displayed normal forms can be computed on these representatives. [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] identifies the resulting coefficient-change maps with the specified derived functors; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies their tensor comparisons with the total-complex comparisons. This does not require a bounded resolution of $B$ or flatness of $B$ over $A$.

The coefficient identification of a single Tate line is the balanced tensor map $((t\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto t\otimes\varphi(a)b$ from $(\mu_N\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A)\otimes_A B$ to $\mu_N\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}B$; its inverse sends $t\otimes b$ to $(t\otimes1)\otimes b$. The balancing relations prove that these are inverse, including for the zero rings. Iterating the same formula gives $A_T(r)\otimes_A B\cong B_T(r)$: on an ordered pure tensor its output is $\bigotimes_{i=1}^r(t_i\otimes1)$ multiplied by $b\prod_i\varphi(a_i)$. At $r=0$ this is $A\otimes_A B\cong B$. Equality on these tensors is equality of sheaf maps by the sheaf-tensor bilinear universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal], applied successively. The root pullbacks in [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] send each $t_i$ to its pullback and are compatible with tensor products and composition; consequently they commute with this coefficient formula term by term. This checks the coefficient-line identification without choosing any global primitive root.

source.place: Section 03EK, bilinear universal property and Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PK for the roots

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] for the geometric inverse images and for the identity-topos ring morphisms $A_T\to B_T$. It gives canonical monoidal pullback compositors computed by ordinary module composition on the representatives of Step 1. The coefficient square for a geometric map commutes because the constant-section map commutes with $\varphi$. Its two ringed-topos paths have the same composite; their canonical comparison is therefore the scalar/pullback comparison. On representatives it moves $b$ across inverse image and sends a tensor to the tensor of its inverse images, with $b$ inserted in the first factor. The coefficient and composition equations of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] assert exactly that these comparisons commute with tensor splitting and with composition, as chain maps. In particular the comparison for $q_rj_r=u_r$ is the pasted comparison $h_r$ followed by $j_{r,B}^*(a_r)$, after the Tate identification of Step 2 and the shifts of Step 4. This identifies the named $a^{u_r}$, rather than merely producing another isomorphism with the same endpoints.

Keep the canonical integer shift maps throughout. [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts] gives the shift-addition laws, the unsigned first-factor comparison, and the second-factor sign $(-1)^{np}$ on a first-factor element of degree $p$. [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-pullback-tensor-shift] says the prescribed pullback tensor comparisons commute with these very maps, for geometric pullback and scalar pullback alike. Every extracted shift here is even, so any second-factor sign is $(-1)^{2rp}=1$, and interchanging extraction of $[2r]$ and $[2]$ has sign $(-1)^{4r}=1$. Termwise inverse image and scalar extension preserve degrees, hence commute with reindexing and with these signs. We may thus combine the successive shifts by $[2r][2]=[2(r+1)]$ in both paths using precisely the canonical shift comparisons, without a residual sign.

source.place: Tag 0FNH, item-shift-tensor in section-sign-rules; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4 for total pullback tensor comparison

proof.text: Unpack the specified ordered right normal form. Write $J_{r,R}:W_{r,R}G_{r,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{r+1,R}$ for its final normalization: first identify $j_r^*q_r^*$ with $u_r^*$, move pullback through the old tensor and shift, identify $u_r^*p_r^*$ with $p_{r+1}^*$, and identify $u_r^*R_{X_r}(r)$ with $R_{X_{r+1}}(r)$ by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Append the new $R(1)$ to the old ordered $r$ factors and reassociate, then add the shifts as in Step 4. These are the canonical pullback/tensor maps of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. By the definition of $I$, $I_{r+1,R}=J_{r,R}\circ W_{r,R}(I_{r,R})$. At zero the unit, identity-pullback and zero-shift identifications give $I_{0,R}=1$. This only spells out the chosen normalization; it makes no new choice of $I$.

source.place: Tags 0D6D and 07A4; the ordered normal-form identification specified in the item, realizing det-sp-reduction-exceptional, Charts, iterated projective-line integration

proof.text:
For this single successor normalization, Steps 2--4 give the square
$$J_{r,B,T_SK}\circ W_{r,B}(a_{r,K})\circ a^{u_r}_{G_{r,A}K}=a_{r+1,K}\circ T_{X_{r+1}}(J_{r,A,K}).$$
Here $a_{r,K}$ denotes the direct comparison indexed by dimension $r$. To check the square explicitly, expand $J$ as in Step 5 on a degree-$m$ element $x$ of the pulled-back $P$, ordered local root tensors $(t_i\otimes a_i)$, and a scalar $b\in B$. Both paths send its scalar part to $b\prod_i\varphi(a_i)$, pull back $x$ along $p_{r+1}$, and retain the root factors in the order $t_1,\ldots,t_r,t_{r+1}$. Each tensor splitting and reassociation commutes with coefficient change by [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]; pullback composition uses the normalized monoidal compositors of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. The Tate pullbacks commute with this formula by Step 2. Pure tensors determine the sheaf maps by [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal], and the even-shift calculation of Step 4 gives the same chain map in every degree. Localizing this equality of chain maps on the representatives of Step 1 proves the displayed equality of the specified derived morphisms. This is one tensor calculation for the final normalization, not an assumption that the full tower already commutes.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 0D6D, representative tensor and composition formulas; more-algebra.tex Tag 0FNH for the signs

proof.text:
Induct on $r$, with claim $I_{r,B}A_r=a_rT(I_{r,A})$ as natural transformations in the input. For $r=0$ both sides are the identity, by the stipulated normalizations. In the following calculation omit component subscripts but retain all functors. The recursion and the induction hypothesis give
$$I_{r+1,B}A_{r+1}=J_{r,B}W_{r,B}(I_{r,B}A_r)a^{u_r}_{\mathcal G_{r,A}}=J_{r,B}W_{r,B}(a_r)W_{r,B}(T(I_{r,A}))a^{u_r}_{\mathcal G_{r,A}}.$$
Naturality of $a^{u_r}$ at $I_{r,A}:\mathcal G_{r,A}\to G_{r,A}$ rewrites the last two factors as $a^{u_r}_{G_{r,A}}T(W_{r,A}(I_{r,A}))$. Apply the successor square of Step 6. The result is
$$a_{r+1}T(J_{r,A})T(W_{r,A}(I_{r,A}))=a_{r+1}T(I_{r+1,A}),$$
which is the claim at $r+1$. This proves the required equality for every $d$ and $K$; all maps were compared in the ordinary etale derived category, and evaluation on the stated $\mathcal C_{S,A}$ inputs gives the assertion.
